objective: Use a full-scale manual separating screen to recover dry ceramic finishing media from an intermixed batch into a collection receiver while retaining every representative steel washer in the screen, then leave the released screen stably resting on both supports. This frozen rigid-PhysX TaskContract specifies later construction; it does not claim native qualification, demonstrated success, occupational-threshold acceptance, or submission readiness.
instruction: Pour the dry mixture into the separating screen. Use the screen to recover the ceramic media in the collection receiver while retaining every metal washer. Return the screen to both supports and release it.
industrial_mapping: Provisional category: Impact on jobs. Raytech source records s-b442a7fa63fcb80c, s-a3efcebbecba0048, and s-855e796b5a3f8ecc establish manual screening as a real dry mass-finishing parts/media separation operation. O*NET record s-474cfcd0ccaa5ecb supports general processed-part inspection and sorting but does not show that finishing-media screening is a regular core duty of an occupation exceeding 500,000 US workers; that mapping remains externally judged and uncertain. The actual tested ability is bimanual loaded-tool control, aperture-mediated separation, bridge release, spill prevention, exact workpiece retention, supported replacement, and release. The completed comparison covered 703 submissions and all six required benchmark suites. Closed/unmerged, other-team PR684 genuinely overlaps with basic apertured sifting but is nonblocking historical evidence under the fixed scope; no current active, accepted, pending, own-team, or benchmark duplicate was identified. Novelty must be refreshed before submission.
damage_rules: At reset freeze media set M as 24 single-body assemblies; washer assemblies WA as four assemblies; washer segments WS(a) as four rigid arc segments per a; WS as their union; and collider-body sets S, R, U, C, G, and T for screen, receiver, supports, feed cup, robot/grippers, and table/floor. Define washer reference x_a(k)=sum_{s in WS(a)}m_s*x_s(k)/sum_{s in WS(a)}m_s and assembly mass m_a=sum_{s in WS(a)}m_s. Count each washer once in admission and F.

Each washer has four authored breakable fixed joints with an assumed 200 N threshold. At completed physics sample k, diagnostic joint force is |J_constraint|/dt from the post-solve constraint impulse, with dt=1/240 s. Actual fracture latches only when PhysX reports a joint broken or formerly connected segments exceed their authored relative transform by 0.0005 m translation or 0.5 deg rotation. Merely reaching 200 N is not damage. Plastic deformation is not modeled, measured, scored, or claimed.

For every completed 240 Hz production step: resolve PhysX; sample transforms, velocities, joint states, signed distances, contacts, and constraint impulses; convert contact or constraint impulse J to step-average force |J|/dt; advance transfer state machines; classify provenance faults; latch immutable events and actual fracture; update containment, recovery, support, clearance, and dwell; then compute score. Process observation O_57600 before timeout. Rendered cameras and public score reporting are sampled at 20 Hz from the latest completed physics sample.

After two seconds of robot-stationary settling, measure an untouched three-second window of 720 completed physics intervals. Translation drift is max_k ||x_S(k)-x_S(start)||; rotation drift is the maximum quaternion geodesic angle; batch speed is max_{b,k}||v_b(k)|| for b in M union WS. Reset every accumulator, state machine, event latch, fracture latch, eligibility flag, and dwell clock between trials.

Define signed penetration p(a,b,k)=max(0,-d_signed(a,b,k)), where negative signed distance denotes overlap and touching is zero. Screen-fixture penetration is max over S versus R union U union T. Dynamic penetration is max where at least one body belongs to M union WS and the other belongs to M union WS union S union R union C union T. Sample every completed 240 Hz post-solve state.

At each 240 Hz sample, screen external force is the sum of magnitudes of post-solve contact impulses over manifold points having exactly one collider in S and the other in G union R union U union C union T union M union WS, divided by dt. Count each unordered collider pair once and exclude S-S contacts. This is physics validation, not grading.

Each intact assembly follows FEED→EXITED_FEED→FREE_FLIGHT→ENTERED_SCREEN. Media use center of mass; intact washers require all segment colliders to satisfy each boundary transition. EXITED_FEED is an outward swept crossing of the cup-mouth plane through its clear opening. FREE_FLIGHT is any later completed sample with the full assembly collider disjoint from cup and screen. ENTERED_SCREEN is a later inward swept crossing of the screen-rim plane through the open top. Multiple free-flight samples are allowed; no adjacent-sample teleport condition is imposed.

Mixture contacts and cup-rim contacts are allowed. Direct robot contact with an individual medium or washer segment, staging-surface contact, receiver entry before genuine screening, non-mouth cup departure, inconsistent intact-washer segment crossing, or unauthorized segment separation before ENTERED_SCREEN is invalid provenance and an immutable score-zero failure. After admission, separation caused by an actual authored-joint break is fracture rather than invalid provenance.

Define full_inside_screen(b,k) by collision geometry, not a point: every vertex of every convex collider belonging to b, transformed at k, must lie in the frozen closed screen containment volume or on its boundary, and no collider may intersect the open-top escape plane outside the inner rim. For a fractured washer this applies independently to every fragment. Define over_rim_exit as a swept collider crossing from full_inside_screen to outside through the open-top plane; crossing is detected if any swept collider vertex or edge intersects that plane outside the inner-rim disk. Thus partial escape is outside and cannot be counted retained.

Washer loss latches when any segment or fragment has an over_rim_exit after admission, contacts T outside R, becomes inaccessible, or crosses below the screen floor without all associated geometry following a genuine clear-aperture path. Media spill latches when a medium exits over the rim, contacts T outside R, enters R without prior genuine aperture passage, exits R after entry, crosses the screen floor outside a clear aperture, becomes inaccessible, intersects a receiver wall, or has invalid provenance. Re-entry never erases an event.

Receiver contamination latches when any washer collider, fragment collider, or other non-media task collider overlaps the receiver interior. Washer loss, media spill, receiver contamination, invalid provenance, and forbidden state mutation are score-zero hard failures. Actual washer fracture alone is not a hard failure: if every fragment remains retained and no hard failure occurs, the final score is permanently capped at 0.40.

The frozen reachable-workspace polytope is P={-0.55<=x<=0.55,-0.05<=y<=0.75,0.05<=z<=0.75} m in table coordinates. A body is inaccessible when any collider vertex is outside P, any collider point lies below z_table-0.02 m, or its full collider lies in a closed fixture volume while all four frozen 0.08 m-square by 0.20 m approach prisms along +z,-x,+x,-y intersect non-target collision meshes. Closed fixture volumes are the solid interiors of R, U, C, and T. A washer is inaccessible if any segment or fragment is inaccessible; IK failure alone is irrelevant.

Any post-reset pose or velocity write to M union WS union S union R union U union C, fake grasp weld, required-collider disable, particle freezing, hidden restoring force, or task-object teleport is a forbidden-state-mutation hard failure. Breakage, spill, loss, excessive contact, and escape must remain physically possible; velocity ceilings, collision suppression, state correction, and hidden return forces may not prevent them.
assets: Independently authored full-scale separating screen. Sourced dimensions: outer diameter 0.3683 m and depth 0.0635 m. Assumptions: 0.003 m floor and wall thickness, 0.150 m perforated-floor radius, 0.0127 m square clear apertures, 0.003 m ribs, 0.0157 m pitch, 0.40 kg mass, and two 0.040 by 0.018 by 0.005 m grasp tabs.

Deterministic screen construction in local coordinates: origin is the floor center; +z is upward; x and y align with aperture sides. The inner wall is a vertical cylinder of radius 0.18115 m from z=0 to z=0.0605 m; the outer wall radius is 0.18415 m and top rim plane is z=0.0635 m. The floor occupies -0.003<=z<=0 except for apertures. Candidate aperture centers are (x_i,y_j)=(0.0157i,0.0157j) m for integer i,j. Include a complete axis-aligned 0.0127 m square aperture iff all four corners have radius <=0.150 m; discard rather than clip boundary squares. Sort polygons lexicographically by i then j, orient vertices counter-clockwise as (x_i-0.00635,y_j-0.00635), (x_i+0.00635,y_j-0.00635), (x_i+0.00635,y_j+0.00635), (x_i-0.00635,y_j+0.00635). Rib/floor collision geometry is the closed floor cylinder minus exactly these through-holes. The containment volume is {-0.003<=z<=0.0635, sqrt(x^2+y^2)<=0.18115} minus rib solids and aperture columns, closed by a scoring-only top disk at z=0.0635; that disk has no collision or force. The published asset must store these generated vertices and polygons for checksum verification.

Twenty-four free rigid ceramic angle-cut cylinders: sourced diameter 0.009525 m and axial envelope 0.022225 m; assumed parallel 15 deg cuts and density 2500 kg/m^3. Record realized closed-mesh mass and inertia; analytic reference mass is 0.0035044969 kg each.

Four representative steel washer assemblies: 0.030 m outer diameter, 0.008 m bore, 0.004 m thickness, density 7850 kg/m^3, four rigid arc segments, and four authored breakable fixed joints. Analytic summed mass is 0.0206170159 kg each. No commercial SKU is claimed.

Rigid receiver with outer dimensions 0.45 by 0.40 by 0.08 m and 0.005 m floor/walls. Its open interior in receiver-local coordinates is -0.220<x<0.220 m, -0.195<y<0.195 m, and 0.005<z<0.075 m. Boundary points are outside. Two support beams are each 0.52 by 0.015 by 0.010 m with four legs. The rigid feed cup has 0.078 m outer diameter, 0.100 m height, 0.003 m floor/walls, and 0.10 kg empty mass.

Pinned public YAM asset and guarded 14D left-seven/right-seven joint-action interface from the hash-indexed runtime snapshots. The pinned scene fixes production physics dt=1/240 s and accepts control_hz=20, giving 12 completed physics intervals per action. A configurable dt is available for prospective 480 Hz refinement.
Industrial sources: Raytech records s-b442a7fa63fcb80c, s-a3efcebbecba0048, and s-855e796b5a3f8ecc; occupational-context record s-474cfcd0ccaa5ecb.
approximations: Only dry rigid-body separation is modeled. Polishing, abrasion, liquid, wet cohesion, dust, wear, lubrication, plastic deformation, and material-property changes are excluded.

Aperture geometry, lattice, ribs, wall profile, screen mass, grasp tabs, media cuts and density, fixtures, representative washer geometry, four-segment fracture proxy, and 200 N joint threshold are disclosed engineering assumptions rather than manufacturer CAD or calibrated commercial specifications.

Initial uncalibrated contacts are ceramic/polymer static/dynamic friction 0.50/0.35, steel/polymer 0.45/0.35, media/media 0.40/0.30, restitution 0.05, contact offset 0.00015 m, rest offset 0 m, and 32/8 solver position/velocity iterations. Force, penetration, drift, joint-margin, clearance, workspace, and approach-corridor limits are validation assumptions requiring independent native tests.

The batch starts entirely in the feed cup; screen and receiver start empty. Assumed planar centers are screen (0,0.25) m and cup (0.31,0.25) m. Support-beam center y values are 0.15 and 0.35 m; support tops and the screen's lowest reset geometry are z=0.13 m above the tabletop.

Clear width is computed directly from each deterministic square aperture polygon; the expected value is 0.0127 m. Construction must verify collision geometry rather than relying only on authored parameters.

End-first trials reset one medium 0.010 m above the center aperture, long axis within 5 deg of floor normal, zero velocity. Passage requires its full collider to cross 0.005 m below the floor through that aperture within two seconds and no continuous rib contact longer than 0.25 s. Use 20 deterministic azimuths with complete resets.

Transverse trials use the same reset with long axis within 5 deg of the floor plane. Bridge-release trials first require no passage for one second, then apply ±4 deg screen roll at 1 Hz for three seconds; release requires genuine aperture passage. These are component tests, not grading requirements.

Washer escape uses 40 deterministic orientations spanning face-on, edge-on, and intermediate attitudes. Bore-lodging uses 20 relative azimuths, two seconds under gravity, a 0.02 m washer lift, and classifies lodging when the medium remains mechanically carried for one second without robot contact.

Bilateral grip requires positive resolved normal-force contact from both opposing finger-collider sides of each gripper against its named grasp tab. Any false 240 Hz sample resets duration. Lift is the minimum world-z point of S minus its settled-reset value. Stationary hold additionally requires all mixture bodies full_inside_screen, lift >=0.030 m, screen speed <=0.010 m/s, and no hard failure.

Joint margins cover every controlled non-fixed robot joint at every 240 Hz sample from the first guarded action through final clearance. Lower margin is q-q_lower and upper margin is q_upper-q; each metric is the minimum over joints and samples.

Camera checks use rendered 20 Hz frames. Valid RGB pixels are finite and within encoded range; valid depth pixels are finite and positive. Required visibility means at least one unoccluded projected pixel for the screen, cup, receiver, one complete medium, and one complete washer, with no identifier overlay.

Refinement replays identical seeds, resets, transforms, action timestamps, and held 20 Hz actions at 240 and 480 Hz for seeds 0 through 4. Recovery delta is the maximum paired absolute final-r difference. Event-type delta is the maximum paired difference in distinct immutable event types. Reset all state between trials.

Scripted experts may read object poses, velocities, joint states, contacts, and scorer flags to plan normal guarded actions. This oracle access does not change model observations and does not permit state writes, teleports, fake welds, collision disablement, particle freezing, or hidden forces.

Construction readiness means native component testing may begin. Passage, bridging, retention, fracture behavior, YAM manipulation, 240/480 Hz agreement, portability, demonstrations, occupational importance, and submission readiness remain unverified.
scoring_spec: Freeze M, WA, WS(a), reset masses, collider sets, deterministic containment geometry, aperture polygons, workspace P, closed fixture meshes, and approach corridors at reset. Let M0=sum_{i in M}m_i+sum_{a in WA}m_a and MM0=sum_{i in M}m_i; count each washer once. valid_admission(b)=1 only after FEED→EXITED_FEED→FREE_FLIGHT→ENTERED_SCREEN completes without a provenance fault. admitted_mass=sum_{i in M}m_i*valid_admission(i)+sum_{a in WA}m_a*valid_admission(a), and F=clamp(admitted_mass/M0,0,1). batch_loaded latches only when all 28 assemblies have valid admission and every current intact collider or fracture fragment is full_inside_screen. A genuine aperture crossing is a downward swept-volume crossing of a medium through z=0 whose plane intersection lies strictly within exactly one frozen aperture polygon and whose swept collider has nonnegative signed distance to every rib; center-only passage is insufficient. eligible_receiver(i,k)=1 iff batch_loaded has latched, i has valid admission, i subsequently completed a genuine aperture crossing, its full collider is currently strictly inside the receiver interior, and it has never spilled, become inaccessible, intersected a receiver wall, or incurred invalid provenance. Define r=clamp(sum_{i in M}m_i*eligible_receiver(i,k)/MM0,0,1). Eligibility is recomputed and revocable every physics sample; immutable faults remain latched. washer_retained requires every current segment or fragment collider to be full_inside_screen; an unfractured washer additionally requires every authored joint intact. supported requires resolved S-U contact on both beams, lowest screen geometry within 0.002 m of support-top z=0.13 m, |roll|<=3 deg, |pitch|<=3 deg, and screen-center projection x in [-0.26,0.26] m and y in [0.15,0.35] m. clear requires minimum signed distance from every G collider to S union M union WS/fragments >=0.060 m. clean means no hard failure. Q=1 iff batch_loaded, F=1, r>=0.98, washer_retained, supported, clear, and clean. Dwell begins at k0 when Q first becomes true; that sample contributes zero elapsed time. D=1 only when Q remains true through k-k0>=720 consecutive completed 240 Hz intervals. Any false prerequisite resets k0 and revokes D. Base score B=0.20F+0.70*clamp(r/0.98,0,1)+0.10D. Final score is 0 after any immutable hard failure; otherwise min(B,0.40) after actual washer fracture and B without fracture. Report at 20 Hz from the latest completed physics sample and process O_57600 before timeout. Initial score is 0; valid complete loading with no recovery is 0.20; exactly 12 of 24 equal-mass media eligible gives 0.5571428571; threshold recovery without dwell gives 0.90; intact valid released dwell gives 1.00. Hand identity, action count, shake count, and prescribed action order are not graded.
